parsed_record.title: Galashin–Lam conjecture on $q,t$-Schur positivity for ${\mathbb Z}$-convex curves
parsed_record.statement:
A curve $C$ passing through lattice points $(0,0)={\bm p}_0,{\bm p}_1,\ldots,{\bm p}_k=(m,n)$ is **${\mathbb Z}$-convex** if the set of lattice points strictly above $C$, together with the points ${\bm p}_i+(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$ for sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, is ${\mathbb Z}$-convex. Write $\operatorname{k}(C)=k$ and let $F_C$ be the symmetric-function invariant associated to $C$. **Galashin–Lam's $q,t$-Schur-positivity conjecture.** For every ${\mathbb Z}$-convex curve $C$, the formal power series

$$
\frac{1}{(1-t)^{\operatorname{k}(C)-1}}F_C
$$

is $q,t$-Schur positive. Here $(1-t)^{-1}=1+t+t^2+\cdots$ is interpreted as a formal power series. This extends the cited conjecture of Blasiak, Haiman, Morse, Pun, and Seelinger; the source gives no resolution.
parsed_record.source_name: Pavel Galashin and Thomas Lam, “Monotone links in DAHA and EHA”, arXiv:2307.16794 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16794

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

parsed_record.title: Terai's conjecture on sequential Cohen–Macaulay edge ideals of weighted graphs
parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a Cohen–Macaulay very well-covered graph, and let $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a standard graded polynomial ring over a field $K$. For a weight function $\mathbf w:E(G)\to\operatorname{\mathbb{Z}}_{>0}$, define the edge ideal

$$
I(G_{\mathbf w})=\big((x_ix_j)^{\mathbf w(x_ix_j)}\mid\{x_i,x_j\}\in E(G)\big)\subseteq S.
$$

**Terai's conjecture.** The ideal $I(G_{\mathbf w})$ is sequentially Cohen–Macaulay for every weight function $\mathbf w$.
This conjecture extends questions about Cohen–Macaulayness and sequential Cohen–Macaulayness of edge ideals of edge-weighted graphs. The source presents it as a conjecture attributed to Terai; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
parsed_record.source_name: Ly Thi Kieu Diem, Nguyen Cong Minh and Thanh Vu, “The sequentially Cohen-Macaulay property of edge ideals of edge-weighted graphs”, arXiv:2308.05020 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05020

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

parsed_record.title: The concise degree-sequence graph-counting conjecture
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathbf d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\in\mathbb N^n$ satisfy $0\le d_i\le n-1$, and let $c(\mathbf d)$ be the number of simple graphs on vertices $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ with $\deg(v_i)=d_i$ for every $i$. **Degree-sequence conciseness conjecture.** For every $k>0$, there exists $\mathbf d$ such that $c(\mathbf d)=k$ and

$$
n\le C(\log k)^c
$$

for some fixed $C,c>0$. The decision problem for graphical degree sequences is polynomial-time decidable, while the conjectured concise value realization is open and can be viewed as a binary symmetric contingency-table problem.
parsed_record.source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Igor Pak, “Computational complexity of counting coincidences”, arXiv:2308.10214 (2024).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10214

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

parsed_record.title: Universal interior conjecture for sums of incommensurable missing digits sets
parsed_record.statement:
Let $A,B\subset[0,1]$ be missing digits sets with bases $p_A$ and $p_B$, and define $T_x(y)=xy$. **Universal interior conjecture.** Suppose that

$$
\frac{\log p_A}{\log p_B}\notin\mathbb{Q}
$$

and

$$
\dim_{\mathrm{H}}A+\dim_{\mathrm{H}}B>1.
$$

Then $A+T_x(B)$ contains a non-trivial interval for every $x\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\\{0\\}$. If $\log p_A/\log p_B\in\mathbb{Q}$, then $A+T_x(B)$ contains a non-trivial interval for every irrational $x$. This is proposed as a stronger, precise form of genericity for sums of missing digits sets; the source presents it as suspected and does not provide a proof.
parsed_record.source_name: Han Yu, “On the absolute continuity of radial and linear projections of missing digits measures”, arXiv:2309.01298 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01298

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

parsed_record.title: King-graph colouring enumeration conjecture
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}_N(4)$ be the set of interlacing triangular arrays of rank $4$ and height $N$. Let $G^{\varhexstar}_N$ be the square king graph with $N+1$ vertices along each side: vertices are adjacent when they differ by a unit horizontal, vertical, or diagonal step. Let $\mathfrak{g}^{\varhexstar}_N(5)$ be the number of proper $5$-colourings of this graph. **King-graph enumeration conjecture.** For every $N\geqslant 1$,

$$
5\,|\mathcal{T}_N(4)|=\mathfrak{g}^{\varhexstar}_N(5).
$$

This is the rank-$4$ analogue of the triangular-graph enumeration claim. The source states that this case remains open; the related rank-$3$ conjecture has a bijective proof.
parsed_record.source_name: Amol Aggarwal, Alexei Borodin and Michael Wheeler, “Coloured corner processes from asymptotics of LLT polynomials”, arXiv:2309.05970 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05970

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “Conjecture has recently been proved bijectively , but Conjecture remains open.”

parsed_record.title: Linear analogue of the product-set dimension inequality
parsed_record.statement:
Let $K\subset L$ be a field extension, and let $A,B\subset L$ be finite-dimensional $K$-subspaces of positive dimension. Suppose that for every $a,b\in L$ and every nontrivial proper finite intermediate subfield $K\subset M\subsetneq L$, one has

$$
\dim_{K}(aM\cap A)+\dim_{K}(bM\cap B)\leq [M:K]+1.
$$

**Linear product-set conjecture.** Then every pair of $K$-subspaces $S\subset A$ and $T\subset B$ satisfies

$$
\dim_{K}\langle ST\rangle\geq \dim_{K}S+\dim_{K}T-1.
$$

This is proposed as a linear analogue of the set-theoretic inequality underlying the matching result in Theorem 1(7), extending the role of the corresponding additive-combinatorial proposition to field extensions.
parsed_record.source_name: Mohsen Aliabadi, “Conditions for matchability in groups and field extensions II”, arXiv:2309.14664 (2024).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.14664

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

parsed_record.title: Generalized Chern number bounds for matroids
parsed_record.statement:
Let $M$ be a simple matroid of rank $d+1$ on a ground set $E$ of size $n$. For nonnegative integers $k_1,\ldots,k_d$ with $k_1+2k_2+\cdots+dk_d=d$, consider the Chern number $\bar{c}_1^{k_1}\cdots \bar{c}_d^{k_d}(M)$ and the corresponding Chern number of the uniform matroid $U_{d+1,n}$. **Generalized Chern number bounds conjecture.** The Chern numbers of $M$ satisfy

$$
|\bar{c}_1^{k_1}\cdots \bar{c}_d^{k_d}(M)| \leq |\bar{c}_1^{k_1}\cdots \bar{c}_d^{k_d}(U_{d+1,n})|.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $M=U_{3,n}$. This conjecture proposes that the upper bounds proved for simple matroids of rank $3$ extend to matroids of arbitrary rank; the supplied text does not provide evidence resolving the conjecture.
parsed_record.source_name: Eline Mannino, “Chern Numbers of Matroids”, arXiv:2310.01956 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01956

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

parsed_record.title: The conjecture that all higher-dimensional grids are stackable
parsed_record.statement:
Let $P_k$ be the path graph on $k$ vertices, let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $k_1,\ldots,k_d$ be positive integers. Write the Cartesian product grid as

$$
\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^d P_{k_i}.
$$

Call a graph **stackable** if, starting with one cup at each vertex, all cups can be moved onto any prescribed target vertex according to the cup-stacking rules. **Grid stackability conjecture.** For all $d$ and $k_1,\ldots,k_d$, the grid

$$
\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^d P_{k_i}
$$

is stackable. The paper establishes the two-dimensional case; stackability in arbitrary grid dimension remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Paul Fay, Glenn Hurlbert and Maya Tennant, “Cup Stacking in Graphs”, arXiv:2310.06192 (2024).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06192

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2023). “Our proof that cubes up to dimension 20 are stackable uses Kleitman's Symmetric Chain Decomposition and the new result of Merino, M\"utze, and Namrata that all generalized Johnson graphs (excluding the Petersen graph) are Hamiltonian.”

parsed_record.title: Kohayakawa–Nagle–Parczyk conjecture on squares of Hamilton cycles in random graphs
parsed_record.statement:
Let $G(n,p)$ be the binomial random graph on vertex set $[n]$, with each possible edge included independently with probability $p=p(n)$. A square of a Hamilton cycle is the second power of a Hamilton cycle: for some cyclic ordering of the vertices, every pair of vertices at cyclic distance at most two is an edge. **Kohayakawa–Nagle–Parczyk conjecture.** For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if

$$
p\geq (1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{e/n},
$$

then $G(n,p)$ a.a.s. contains a square of a Hamilton cycle. This is a more precise proposed sufficient condition than the earlier threshold prediction; the supplied passage does not state whether it has been resolved.
parsed_record.source_name: Yulin Chang, Jie Han and Lin Sun, “The threshold for powers of tight Hamilton cycles in random hypergraphs”, arXiv:2310.18980 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18980

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

parsed_record.title: Speyer's non-negativity conjecture for matroid g-polynomials
parsed_record.statement: Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a matroid, and let $g_{\mathsf{M}}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ denote its $g$-polynomial. **Speyer's conjecture.** For every matroid $\mathsf{M}$, the polynomial $g_{\mathsf{M}}(t)$ has non-negative coefficients. This conjecture concerns positivity of the covaluative $g$-polynomial, which is known in the source for the Schubert-matroid setting but is asserted here for arbitrary matroids; its general resolution status is not specified.
parsed_record.source_name: Luis Ferroni, “Schubert matroids, Delannoy paths, and Speyer's invariant”, arXiv:2311.01397 (2023).

parsed_record.title: The feasibility conjecture for finite abelian groups
parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. A finite abelian group is called $(|G|-1)$-close when every relevant block-matroid labeling satisfies the corresponding closeness condition.

**Feasibility conjecture.** Every finite abelian group $G$ is $(|G|-1)$-close.

This conjecture concerns the feasibility threshold for congruency-constrained matroid bases. The paper states that it makes progress toward the conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence. It should not be confused with the earlier, stronger claim involving $D(G)-1$, which the paper says was recently disproved.
parsed_record.source_name: Siyue Liu and Chao Xu, “On the Congruency-Constrained Matroid Base”, arXiv:2311.11737 (2024).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.11737

parsed_record.title: Chow–Taylor conjecture on Latin wide Young diagrams
parsed_record.statement: A Young diagram $Y$ is **wide** if, for every subset $S$ of its rows, the diagram formed by $S$ dominates its conjugate; a filling of $Y$ is **Latin** if it assigns to each row the numbers $1,\ldots,a_i$ injectively and is also injective in every column. **Chow–Taylor's conjecture.** If a Young diagram $Y$ is wide, then it is Latin. This is the converse of the theorem that every Latin Young diagram is wide; the paper states that it proves a weaker dual version, so the converse remains the conjectural claim considered here.
parsed_record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, He Guo and Daniel Kotlar, “2-covers of wide Young diagrams”, arXiv:2311.17670 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

parsed_record.title: Conjecture on the number of ideals in C-vines
parsed_record.statement:
Let a C-vine have dimension $\ell
greater than or equal to1$, and let $N_\ell$ denote its number of ideals.

**C-vine ideal-count conjecture.** The number of ideals in the C-vine of dimension $\ell\ge1$ is given by the OEIS sequence A047970:

$$
N_\ell=\sum_{i=0}^\ell\left((i+1)^{\ell-i}-i^{\ell-i}\right).
$$

This conjecture arises from calculations for C-vines. The general problem of counting ideals in arbitrary R-vines is stated to remain open, while the corresponding count for D-vines is known to be the Catalan number.
parsed_record.source_name: Hung Manh Tran, Tan Nhat Tran and Shuhei Tsujie, “Vines and MAT-labeled graphs”, arXiv:2311.17793 (2024).

parsed_record.title: The C3-free graph bound for positive Lin-Lu-Yau Ricci curvature
parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $C_3$-free graph. For every edge $xy$ in $G$, suppose that $\kappa_{\textrm{LLY}}(x,y)\geq \kappa>0$.

**The C3-free curvature bound.** Then

$$
|V(G)|\leq 2^{2/\kappa}.
$$

This conjecture extends the proved bound for connected graphs containing neither $C_3$ nor $C_5$ to all connected triangle-free graphs. The stated material does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
parsed_record.source_name: E. G. K. M. Gamlath, Xiaonan Liu, Linyuan Lu and Xiaofan Yuan, “A tight bound on \C_3,C_5\-free connected graphs with positive Lin-Lu-Yau Ricci curvature”, arXiv:2312.16593 (2023).
parsed_record.references:

parsed_record.title: Degenerate tiling incidence conjecture over division rings
parsed_record.statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a **simple tiling** of a surface of positive genus, meaning that its underlying graph is $(n+1)$-degenerate, and let ${\mathrm D}$ be a division ring. The incidence theorem corresponding to $\mathcal T$ is an incidence statement in projective space $\mathbb{P}^n({\mathrm D})$. **Degenerate tiling incidence conjecture.** The incidence theorem corresponding to $\mathcal T$ holds in $\mathbb{P}^n({\mathrm D})$ if and only if ${\mathrm D}$ is commutative. This would extend the preceding argument from the specific tiling considered there to all simple $(n+1)$-degenerate tilings of positive-genus surfaces; combined with bounds on the degeneracy of graphs embeddable in a fixed genus, it would imply corresponding dimension thresholds for all simple tilings of a fixed positive genus.
parsed_record.source_name: Anton Izosimov, “Surface topology and incidence theorems over division rings”, arXiv:2603.00288 (2026).
parsed_record.references:

parsed_record.title: Cactus-shadow extension conjecture for the necklace formula
parsed_record.statement:
Let an embedded shadow have a block-adjacency graph that is a cactus, meaning that any two cyclic blocks share at most one vertex, and suppose that its cyclic blocks are annular in the sense of the source's necklace definition. The attached tree-like components may have arbitrary nesting, and Shapiro's local admissibility conditions are understood relative to the actual nesting of the building polygons.

**Cactus-shadow extension conjecture.** For any embedded shadow whose block-adjacency graph is a cactus and whose cyclic blocks are annular in the sense of the necklace definition, the formula of the source's necklace theorem remains valid even when the attached tree-like components have arbitrary nesting, provided that Shapiro's local admissibility conditions are interpreted with respect to the actual nesting of the building polygons.

This would extend the known tree--necklace formula beyond the previously treated nesting configurations. The supplied text identifies arbitrary nesting and global compatibility as remaining issues, and gives no evidence that the extension has been proved.
parsed_record.source_name: Boris Shapiro, “Combinatorics of Inflection Points of Plane Curve Shadows”, arXiv:2605.27471 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27471

parsed_record.title: Reversal-Wilf conjecture for contraction containment in labeled trees
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal T_m$ denote the set of labeled trees on $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. For $T\in\mathcal T_n$ and $U\in\mathcal T_m$, write $T\preceq U$ if $U$ displays $T$, meaning that $T$ can be obtained from $U$ by contracting connected fibers and then standardizing the survivor labels. Define the support count by

$$
\mu_T(m)=\#\{U\in\mathcal T_m:T\preceq U\}.
$$

Let $R_n$ be label reversal, $i\mapsto n+1-i$. **Reversal-Wilf conjecture.** For $T_1,T_2\in\mathcal T_n$, if

$$
\mu_{T_1}(m)=\mu_{T_2}(m)\qquad(m\ge n),
$$

then $T_2=T_1$ or $T_2=R_n(T_1)$. Reversal of the ambient label set already gives $\mu_T(m)=\mu_{R_n(T)}(m)$ for all $m$, so the conjecture asserts that these are the only equal support-count sequences. It asks whether contraction containment among labeled trees has no Wilf-equivalences beyond label reversal.
parsed_record.source_name: Levi Segal, “Structure, Enumeration, and star avoidance for contraction containment in labeled trees”, arXiv:2606.07668 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07668

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

parsed_record.title: Frankl–Kiselev–Kupavskii conjecture on symmetric differences of intersecting families
parsed_record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ denote the family of all $k$-element subsets of $[n]$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ is **intersecting** if $F\cap F'\neq\emptyset$ for all $F,F'\in\mathcal{F}$. For sets $F,G$, write $F\triangle G=(F\cup G)\setminus(F\cap G)$, and define

$$
\mathcal{SD}(\mathcal{F})=\{F\triangle G:F,G\in\mathcal{F}\}.
$$

**Frankl–Kiselev–Kupavskii conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ is intersecting and $n>10k$, then

$$
|\mathcal{SD}(\mathcal{F})|\le\sum_{\ell=0}^{k-1}\binom{n-1}{2\ell}.
$$

The right-hand side is attained by a full star, so the conjecture asserts that full stars maximize the number of symmetric differences among intersecting $k$-uniform families in the stated range. The supplied text gives the conjecture's origin but no resolution, so its status is open.
parsed_record.source_name: Lihua Feng, Zejun Huang, Qifan Wang and Yongjiang Wu, “Improved bound on symmetric differences of intersecting families”, arXiv:2606.20043 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20043

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

parsed_record.title: Balogh–Lidický–Mubayi–Pfender–Volec upper-profile conjecture for the red-blue star
parsed_record.statement:
Let $S_{2,1}$ be the red-blue star with one distinguished centre, two ordered red leaves, and one blue leaf. For $\beta\text{ in }[0,1]$, define

$$
s(\beta)=\max\{xy^2(1-y)+y(x+y)^2(1-x-y):x,y\geq 0,\ x+y\leq 1,\ 2xy+y^2=\beta\}.
$$

Here $I(S_{2,1},\beta)$ denotes the fixed-density upper profile of $S_{2,1}$.

**Balogh–Lidický–Mubayi–Pfender–Volec's upper-profile conjecture.** There exists $y\in(0,1/4)$ such that, for every $\beta\in[0,1]$,

$$
I(S_{2,1},\beta)=\begin{cases}s(\beta),&0\leq\beta\leq y,\\[1mm]\beta^{3/2}(1-\sqrt{\beta}),&y\leq\beta\leq 1/4,\\[1mm]\beta/4,&1/4\leq\beta\leq 1/2,\\[1mm]\beta^2(1-\beta),&1/2\leq\beta\leq 1.\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture describes the full upper fixed-density profile: the low-density regime is governed by the function $s$, while the denser regimes are given by explicit constructions. The supplied text subsequently states a theorem proving the profile with the transition at $t_*^2$, so this conjecture is solved in the paper.
parsed_record.source_name: Jinghua Deng and Jianfeng Hou, “Fixed-density profiles for the semi-induced 4-vertex star”, arXiv:2606.23351 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23351

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed_record.title: The genus-three formula conjecture for the coefficients $S_{n,k}^{(3)}$
parsed_record.statement: Let $S_{n,k}^{(g)}$ denote the coefficients indexed by $n$, $k$, and genus $g$, and let the expression referred to as $$ be the proposed formula for these coefficients. **Genus-three formula conjecture.** The expression $$, with $g=3$, gives $S_{n,k}^{(3)}$ for all $n$ and $k$. The formula agrees with all presently known experimental values and its sum over $k$ agrees with $B_n^{(3)}$; its validity beyond the tested range remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Robert Coquereaux and Jean-Bernard Zuber, “Counting partitions by genus: a compendium of results”, arXiv:2305.01100 (2024).
